31.1: The words of King Lemuel, an oracle that his mother taught him:
31.2: O my son, O son of my womb, O son of my vows,
31.3: do not give your strength to women, nor your ways to that which ruins kings.
31.4: It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine or for rulers to crave strong drink,
31.5: lest they drink and forget what is decreed and remove from all the poor their legal rights.
31.6: Give strong drink to the one who is perishing and wine to those who are bitterly distressed;
31.7: let them drink and forget their poverty, and remember their misery no more.
31.8: Open your mouth on behalf of those unable to speak, for the legal rights of all the dying.
31.9: Open your mouth, judge in righteousness, and plead the cause of the poor and needy.
31.10: Who can find a wife of noble character? For her value is far more than rubies.
31.11: Her husband’s heart has trusted her, and he does not lack the dividends.
31.12: She has rewarded him with good and not harm all the days of her life.
31.13: She sought out wool and flax, then worked happily with her hands.
31.14: She was like the merchant ships; she would bring in her food from afar.
31.15: Then she rose while it was still night, and provided food for her household and a portion to her female servants.
31.16: She considered a field and bought it; from her own income she planted a vineyard.
31.17: She clothed herself in might, and she strengthened her arms.
31.18: She perceived that her merchandise was good. Her lamp would not go out in the night.
31.19: She extended her hands to the spool, and her hands grasped the spindle.
31.20: She opened her hand to the poor, and extended her hands to the needy.
31.21: She would not fear for her household in winter, because all her household were clothed with scarlet,
31.22: because she had made coverings for herself; and because her clothing was fine linen and purple.
31.23: Her husband is well known in the city gate when he sits with the elders of the land.
31.24: She made linen garments then sold them and traded belts to the merchants;
31.25: her clothing was strong and splendid; and she laughed at the time to come.
31.26: She has opened her mouth with wisdom, with loving instruction on her tongue.
31.27: Watching over the ways of her household, she would not eat the bread of idleness.
31.28: Her children have risen and called her blessed; her husband also has praised her:
31.29: “Many daughters have done valiantly, but you have surpassed them all!”
31.30: Charm is deceitful and beauty is fleeting. A woman who fears the Lord—she makes herself praiseworthy.
31.31: Give her credit for what she has accomplished, and let her works praise her in the city gates.

31.1: The sayings of King Lemuel contain this message, which his mother taught him.
31.2: O my son, O son of my womb, O son of my vows,
31.3: do not waste your strength on women, on those who ruin kings.
31.4: It is not for kings, O Lemuel, to guzzle wine. Rulers should not crave alcohol.
31.5: For if they drink, they may forget the law and not give justice to the oppressed.
31.6: Alcohol is for the dying, and wine for those in bitter distress.
31.7: Let them drink to forget their poverty and remember their troubles no more.
31.8: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves; ensure justice for those being crushed.
31.9: Yes, speak up for the poor and helpless, and see that they get justice.
31.10: Who can find a virtuous and capable wife? She is more precious than rubies.
31.11: Her husband can trust her, and she will greatly enrich his life.
31.12: She brings him good, not harm, all the days of her life.
31.13: She finds wool and flax and busily spins it.
31.14: She is like a merchant’s ship, bringing her food from afar.
31.15: She gets up before dawn to prepare breakfast for her household and plan the day’s work for her servant girls.
31.16: She goes to inspect a field and buys it; with her earnings she plants a vineyard.
31.17: She is energetic and strong, a hard worker.
31.18: She makes sure her dealings are profitable; her lamp burns late into the night.
31.19: Her hands are busy spinning thread, her fingers twisting fiber.
31.20: She extends a helping hand to the poor and opens her arms to the needy.
31.21: She has no fear of winter for her household, for everyone has warm clothes.
31.22: She makes her own bedspreads. She dresses in fine linen and purple gowns.
31.23: Her husband is well known at the city gates, where he sits with the other civic leaders.
31.24: She makes belted linen garments and sashes to sell to the merchants.
31.25: She is clothed with strength and dignity, and she laughs without fear of the future.
31.26: When she speaks, her words are wise, and she gives instructions with kindness.
31.27: She carefully watches everything in her household and suffers nothing from laziness.
31.28: Her children stand and bless her. Her husband praises her:
31.29: “There are many virtuous and capable women in the world, but you surpass them all!”
31.30: Charm is deceptive, and beauty does not last; but a woman who fears the Lord will be greatly praised.
31.31: Reward her for all she has done. Let her deeds publicly declare her praise.

31.1: The words of King Lemuel, the strong advice his mother gave him:
31.2: “Oh, son of mine, what can you be thinking of! Child whom I bore! The son I dedicated to God! Don’t dilute your strength on fortune-hunting women, promiscuous women who shipwreck leaders.
31.4: “Leaders can’t afford to make fools of themselves, gulping wine and swilling beer, Lest, hung over, they don’t know right from wrong, and the people who depend on them are hurt. Use wine and beer only as sedatives, to kill the pain and dull the ache Of the terminally ill, for whom life is a living death.
31.8: “Speak up for the people who have no voice, for the rights of all the misfits. Speak out for justice! Stand up for the poor and destitute!”
31.10: A good woman is hard to find, and worth far more than diamonds. Her husband trusts her without reserve, and never has reason to regret it. Never spiteful, she treats him generously all her life long. She shops around for the best yarns and cottons, and enjoys knitting and sewing. She’s like a trading ship that sails to faraway places and brings back exotic surprises. She’s up before dawn, preparing breakfast for her family and organizing her day. She looks over a field and buys it, then, with money she’s put aside, plants a garden. First thing in the morning, she dresses for work, rolls up her sleeves, eager to get started. She senses the worth of her work, is in no hurry to call it quits for the day. She’s skilled in the crafts of home and hearth, diligent in homemaking. She’s quick to assist anyone in need, reaches out to help the poor. She doesn’t worry about her family when it snows; their winter clothes are all mended and ready to wear. She makes her own clothing, and dresses in colorful linens and silks. Her husband is greatly respected when he deliberates with the city fathers. She designs gowns and sells them, brings the sweaters she knits to the dress shops. Her clothes are well-made and elegant, and she always faces tomorrow with a smile. When she speaks she has something worthwhile to say, and she always says it kindly. She keeps an eye on everyone in her household, and keeps them all busy and productive. Her children respect and bless her; her husband joins in with words of praise: “Many women have done wonderful things, but you’ve outclassed them all!” Charm can mislead and beauty soon fades. The woman to be admired and praised is the woman who lives in the Fear-of-God. Give her everything she deserves! Adorn her life with praises!

31.10: Who shall find a virtuous woman? for such a one is more valuable than precious stones.
31.11: The heart of her husband trusts in her: such a one shall stand in no need of fine spoils.
31.12: For she employs all her living for her husband's good.
31.13: Gathering wool and flax, she makes it serviceable with her hands.
31.14: She is like a ship trading from a distance: so she procures her livelihood.
31.15: And she rises by night, and gives food to her household, and appointed tasks to her maidens.
31.16: She views a farm, and buys it: and with the fruit of her hands she plants a possession.
31.17: She strongly girds her loins, and strengthens her arms for work.
31.18: And she finds by experience that working is good; and her candle goes not out all night.
31.19: She reaches forth her arms to needful works, and applies her hands to the spindle.
31.20: And she opens her hands to the needy, and reaches out fruit to the poor.
31.21: Her husband is not anxious about those at home when he tarries anywhere abroad: for all her household are clothed.
31.22: She makes for her husband clothes of double texture, and garments for herself of fine linen and scarlet.
31.23: And her husband becomes a distinguished person in the gates, when he sits in council with the old inhabitants of the land.
31.24: She makes fine linens, and sells girdles to the Chananites: she opens her mouth heedfully and with propriety, and controls her tongue.
31.25: She puts on strength and honour; and rejoices in the last days.
31.26: The ways of her household are careful, and she eats not the bread of idleness.
31.27: But she opens her mouth wisely, and according to law.
31.28: And her kindness to them sets up her children for them, and they grow rich, and her husband praises her.
31.29: Many daughters have obtained wealth, many have wrought valiantly; but thou hast exceeded, thou hast surpassed all.
31.30: Charms are false, and woman's beauty is vain: for it is a wise woman that is blessed, and let her praise the fear of the Lord.
31.31: Give her of the fruit of her lips; and let her husband be praised in the gates.
